name: Kairn + Headroom Competitive Learning And Combo Evaluation
description: Research manifest for comparing direct baseline, Headroom-only compression, Kairn-only governance, and Kairn-plus-Headroom composition.

arms.description: Codex/agent run with no Kairn and no Headroom.
Headroom proxy path with optimization disabled, used to isolate proxy-hop cost.
Headroom compression/proxy/wrapper enabled without Kairn governance.
Existing Kairn Codex-session or real MCP mode.
Kairn selects/governs context first; Headroom compresses downstream noisy payloads/tool output where feasible.

smokeChecks.note: SDK client listed tools and completed compress/retrieve/stats round trip.
Attribution survived; Headroom nooped because Kairn payload was already tiny.
Headroom compressed 3633 estimated tokens to 63 while preserving src/runtime/KairnRuntime.ts and retrieval.

smokeChecks.command: Kairn MCP payload matrix plus Headroom-only raw noisy output -> headroom_compress/headroom_retrieve
smokeChecks.note: Seven payloads completed. Kairn+Headroom saved 14,947 of 22,202 tokens across six local payloads, with zero lost-attribution rows. Headroom-only raw noisy output saved 10,180 of 11,673 tokens.
Headroom protected a 133,141-token broad source bundle as recent code and did not compress it, preserving attribution but not reducing prompt pressure.
The wrapper launched Codex, but it injected a Headroom provider into the live Codex config. The backup was restored; future live tests should isolate CODEX_HOME.

smokeChecks.command: Direct Codex tiny prompt vs headroom wrap codex tiny prompt with isolated CODEX_HOME
smokeChecks.note: Direct Codex reported 12917 input / 24 output tokens. Headroom-wrapped Codex reported 12880 input / 25 output tokens and returned the same response. This proves accounting stability, not meaningful savings.

smokeChecks.command: Noisy parser fixture across baseline_direct, headroom_passthrough, kairn_only, and kairn_plus_headroom
smokeChecks.note: All four arms passed quality. Codex-observed input tokens: baseline 68854, Headroom 82098, Kairn 68591, Kairn+Headroom 131762. The Headroom proxy wrapper path is not promising for this coding row.

smokeChecks.command: Full noisy failure-output prompt vs Kairn failure-context prompt after Headroom compression attempt
smokeChecks.note: Both arms passed. Full-log prompt observed 85176 input tokens. Kairn failure context prompt observed 56105 input tokens. Headroom nooped on Kairn output, so this supports Kairn-first compression rather than Headroom-added savings.

smokeChecks.command: Kairn MCP selected payloads -> Headroom MCP compression and retrieval
smokeChecks.note: Kairn+Headroom MCP rows compressed 26,755 -> 6,785 tokens, saving 19,970 tokens (74.6%) with zero lost-attribution rows.

smokeChecks.command: Raw baseline vs Headroom-only vs Kairn-only vs Kairn+Headroom across source-bearing MCP scenarios
smokeChecks.note: Six source-bearing rows preserved attribution. Combo was best on 4/6 rows, reduced aggregate tokens 95.3% vs baseline, and was 85.5% lower than Kairn-only on aggregate. Heavy lifting was Kairn-led on 4/6 rows.

plannedLiveRows.gate: Run only after passthrough and token accounting smoke are stable.
Kairn must keep source attribution before Headroom compression is applied.
Most likely combo win class; requires quality pass and valid token accounting.
Stop if compression hides route/component/test ownership evidence.
